parole.significato: Money in the form of notes or bills and coins, as opposed to checks, credit or electronic transactions.
parole.testo: From late Middle French caisse (“money-box”), itself borrowed from Occitan caissa, from Latin capsa (“box”), ultimately from capiō (“take, seize”), from Proto-Indo-European *kap- (“grasp”). Doublet of case, chase, and chasse. Compare Spanish caja (“box”).

parole.significato: A piece of harness used on a horse to keep it from raising its head above a desired point.
parole.testo: From Middle French martingale, from Occitan martegalo, feminine form of martegal, an inhabitant of Martigues, which is from Latin maritima. Possibly merged with Spanish almártaga. The meaning in gambling may come from an old usage of à la martingale to mean absurdly or foolishly.https://people.math.

parole.significato: A strong cold north-west wind in southern France and the Mediterranean.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Middle French mistral, from Occitan. Doublet of magistral.
